descriptionChirho: A natural or rock-hewn hollow (σπήλαιον) used as a shelter, hideout, or lair, appearing in both singular ('a cave/den') and plural ('caves') forms. In the NT, used for the 'den of robbers' (quoting Jeremiah via Jesus's temple cleansing), burial caves, and apocalyptic hiding places. Multilingual evidence is consistent across number: Arabic مَغارَة (singular)/كُهُوف (plural), Korean 굴/굴들, Swahili pango/mapango, Hindi गुफा/गुफाओं, Spanish cueva/cuevas. The singular and plural represent grammatical number inflection of a single lexical sense, not distinct meanings.
